newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota profit jumps 50 percent in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Toyota profit jumps 50 percent in 1996/97.

text.p: Giant Japanese carmaker Toyota Motor Corp on Wednesday announced a hefty increase of over 50 percent in its group profit last business year.

The weak yen and cost-cutting helped boost the carmaker's group net profit by 50.2 percent to 385.92 billion yen ($3.41 billion) in the year to March 1997. Net profit is equal to current profit, which is pre-tax, minus taxes and extraordinary profits and losses.

On a parent basis, the nation's biggest carmaker said its current profit jumped 82.1 percent to 620.41 billion yen ($5.49 billion) last business year. It predicted profits would grow further to 630 billion yen ($5.57 billion) this year. Current profit is pre-tax and includes losses or gains on investments.

But the profit estimate was much smaller than analysts had expected. They had estimated that Toyota's 1997/98 profit should surpass its largest ever level of 733.80 billion yen ($6.49 billion), marked in the year which ended on June 30, 1990.

Behind Toyota's rosy earnings result was the yen's weakness, which galvanised the carmaker's overseas sales. The Japanese currency averaged 113.34 to the dollar in 1996/97 against 96.80 the year before.

Rival automaker Honda Motor Co Ltd also announced a jump in profits this week, saying on Tuesday that its group net profit more than tripled in the last business year thanks to the weaker yen. ($1=113 yen)
